name: VALORANT
notes: Vanguard protects VALORANT at the kernel level, so Framecalm never touches its files or its process. These are the exact in-game steps.

guided.where: Settings > Video > General > Limit FPS Always
guided.set: Off, or your monitor's refresh rate
guided.why: A low cap is the most common reason VALORANT feels slower than it should.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Graphics Quality > Multithreaded Rendering
guided.why: Spreads work across CPU cores. VALORANT is usually CPU-limited.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Graphics Quality > Material / Texture / Detail Quality
guided.why: Big gains on integrated and laptop GPUs, barely visible in fights.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Graphics Quality > Vignette, Bloom, Distortion, Cast Shadows
guided.why: Pure effects. Off is also easier to read.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Graphics Quality > NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
guided.why: Lowers input delay when the GPU is the limit.

name: Counter-Strike 2
notes: CS2 settings live in Steam Cloud and the game rewrites them, so guided steps are more reliable here.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Advanced Video > Boost Player Contrast
guided.why: Keeps players readable when you lower other settings.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Advanced Video > Shader Detail / Particle Detail
guided.why: Smokes and molotovs are the biggest frame-time spikes in CS2.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Advanced Video > Ambient Occlusion, Depth of field
guided.why: Effects with a clear cost and no gameplay value.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Advanced Video > Max Frames Per Second
guided.set: 0 (unlimited) or a bit above your refresh rate
guided.why: Low caps throw frames away.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Advanced Video > NVIDIA Reflex
guided.why: Lower input delay when GPU-limited.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Texture Streaming Budget
guided.set: One step below your VRAM (e.g. Medium for 4 GB)
guided.why: Running out of VRAM causes the worst stutters in Apex.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Sun Shadow Coverage / Detail, Spot Shadow Detail
guided.why: Shadows are the heaviest setting group.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Volumetric Lighting, Dynamic Spot Shadows
guided.why: Large GPU cost, little gameplay value.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Adaptive Resolution FPS Target
guided.why: Keeps the image sharp; tune with real settings instead.

guided.where: Options > Video > Frame Rate
guided.set: Custom, at or above your refresh rate
guided.why: The default cap can be lower than your screen.

guided.where: Options > Video > Graphics Quality > Shadow Detail
guided.why: Biggest single GPU cost.

guided.where: Options > Video > Graphics Quality > Local Fog Detail, Dynamic Reflections
guided.why: Heavy effects in busy fights.

guided.where: Options > Video > NVIDIA Reflex
guided.why: Lower input delay.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Frame Rate Cap
guided.why: The default cap can be lower than your screen.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Shadow Quality
guided.why: Shadows are the main GPU cost in team fights.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Effects Quality
guided.why: Ability effects spike frame times in fights.

guided.where: Settings > Video > Wait for Vertical Sync
guided.why: Removes the V-Sync cap and its delay.

guided.where: Options > Graphics > Shadow Quality
guided.why: Big GPU cost.

guided.where: Options > Graphics > Ambient Occlusion, Lens Effects, Zoom-in Depth of Field
guided.why: Effects with little gameplay value.

guided.where: Options > Display > V-Sync
guided.why: Removes the cap and its input delay.

guided.where: Settings > Graphics > Shadows, Effects, Foliage
guided.why: The heaviest groups. Very Low foliage also helps spotting.

guided.where: Settings > Graphics > View Distance
guided.why: CPU-heavy in towns. Medium keeps far players visible.

guided.where: Settings > Graphics > Frame Rate Limit
guided.why: Default caps can be low.

name: Roblox
notes: Roblox protects its client with Hyperion, so Framecalm never touches its files or its process, and doesn't use FPS unlockers or client flags. These are the exact in-game steps.

guided.where: Esc > Settings > Maximum Frame Rate
guided.why: Roblox defaults to 60. This is the official setting, no unlocker needed.

guided.where: Esc > Settings > Graphics Mode
guided.why: Automatic often picks a higher quality than your PC can hold.

guided.where: Esc > Settings > Graphics Quality
guided.set: 3 to 5 bars on laptops, then raise it until FPS drops
guided.why: Each bar adds render distance, shadows and effects. It's the biggest lever in Roblox.

guided.where: Esc > Settings > Fullscreen
guided.why: Fullscreen avoids extra work Windows does for windowed apps on some PCs.
